gate: Phase 6 slice 6 — startAtSec actually moves a real video
why: startAtSec is the mechanism that makes the watch-to-review loop a loop rather than a list: it is what takes a struggling Anki card back to the exact line it was mined from. It was unit-tested end to end but had NEVER moved a real video. This closes that.
driver: the app's own debug bridge on 127.0.0.1:39273 — no Windows mouse or keyboard control

environment.SEANIME_DATADIR: C:/Users/Arseniy/AppData/Local/Temp/seanime-phase3-gplay-20260728 — the isolated G-PLAY fixture profile, deliberately NOT the real <userData>/seanime
environment.sidecar: ready, v3.10.2, port 50916, pid 8140 (ports are ephemeral — see the port-mismatch finding below)
environment.fixture: cue-library/Sousou no Frieren - 01.mkv, 11,873,146 bytes, duration 30.386s, dual ASS subtitle tracks
environment.screenshot: startatsec-replay-12.5s.png — documents the live environment (sidecar panel showing the isolated datadir, real player, full study dock). The landing itself is evidenced by the capture-phase media-event logs below, not by the still.

method: A capture-phase document listener recorded loadedmetadata/play/seeking/seeked with video.currentTime, rather than polling. The replay request is the app's own `seanime:media-workspace-open` event carrying { localFilePath, startAtSec } — deliberately not pickMedia(), whose native dialog a bridge-driven run cannot answer.
discriminator: The resume store already held a position for this exact file from the earlier G-PLAY run: jp-video-core-resume-v1 = positionSec 3.566411. So 'startAtSec was honoured' and 'the stored resume was honoured' predict different, distinguishable landings.

runs.verdict: landed at 12.5, NOT at the stored 3.566
landed at 25.0, NOT at the stored 22.2 — a second, different supplied value, so the mechanism tracks the parameter rather than a constant
reproduced exactly on a third run

conclusion: Three runs, two distinct supplied values, each landing on the supplied value to within 15 ms, each overriding a different stored resume position. startAtSec moves a real video.

openQuestionFoundHere.what: Reopening the SAME already-active file with NO startAtSec did not apply the stored resume position — it restarted at 0 and played forward.
openQuestionFoundHere.evidenceItIsNotAMeasurementError: The store was planted with positionSec 8.8 under the exact key the app itself writes (file:c:/users/.../sousou no frieren - 01.mkv), and re-read immediately before dispatch to confirm the ResumeTracker had not overwritten it. It still read 8.8. The video logged play ct=0.017 and played forward to 7.178.
openQuestionFoundHere.notARegressionFromThisSlice: The no-startAtSec path is byte-identical to before the change: `requestedSec ?? (…loadResumePosition(nativeInfo)…)` falls through to the same call with the same argument when startAtSec is absent.
openQuestionFoundHere.andResumeIsKnownToWorkElsewhere: proof/gplay-20260730 recorded `play t=6 -> seeking t=6 -> seeked t=6` after a real app RESTART, i.e. on a cold player mount. The failing case here is a reopen while the player is already active on that same file.
openQuestionFoundHere.status: MEASURED BUT UNEXPLAINED. Deliberately not diagnosed further from a single probe, and deliberately not written up as 'resume is broken' — that is the one-probe-conclusion error this track has made before. Next step if it matters: reopen after a full app restart, and instrument loadResumePosition's return value directly.

twoEnvironmentFindings.what: The sidecar port is ephemeral AND the renderer's connection can be stale against it. A first attempt produced a permanently idle player: the renderer logged 'WebsocketSender … socket state: null' and window.api.seanimeConnection() reported baseUrl port 50916 while seanimeStatus() reported 60938.
twoEnvironmentFindings.sequenceThatWorks: start the sidecar -> reload the renderer -> re-read BOTH seanimeStatus().port and seanimeConnection().baseUrl and require them to AGREE -> only then dispatch the open. Do not trust either one alone.

twoEnvironmentFindings.what: The debug bridge's /eval takes its code in a field named `js`, not `code`. A wrong field name returns { ok:false, error:'missing js' }, which reads like a bridge fault rather than a caller mistake.
twoEnvironmentFindings.alsoConfirmed: /screenshot WRITES a PNG to debug/shots/ and returns { ok, path, size } as JSON. Piping the response body to a .png file yields a 137-byte JSON file, not an image.
